model_reported.summary: Proposed a four-row-per-thread mapping while retaining the baseline CTA output footprint, so the comparison isolates thread mapping and register blocking.

model_reported.summary: Used the supplied GH200 and CUDA 12.6.3 target facts; no additional environment inspection was needed for this ordinary SIMT kernel.

model_reported.summary: The experiment uses standard CUDA kernel indexing and FP32 arithmetic, with no uncertain APIs or architecture-specific instructions.

model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Recorded the valid measured baseline as the control and did not infer candidate speed or correctness before controller evaluation.

proposal.hypothesis: The baseline assigns one output to each thread in a 32x32 CTA, with neighboring lanes advancing across rows and therefore accessing row-major A and C with strides. This candidate keeps the same 32x32 output footprint but maps lanes across columns and assigns four rows at one column to each thread. That reuses each loaded B value across four independent FP32 accumulators and may improve coalescing while reducing CTA threads from 1024 to 256; the additional per-thread state may affect occupancy. The baseline is the measured one-output-per-thread control; candidate performance remains unmeasured.

retained: Map each CTA to the same 32x32 output tile as the baseline using a 32x8 block; each thread computes four rows at one column.
Maintain four independent FP32 accumulators per thread and reuse the per-K B value across those outputs; lane columns access B and C contiguously.
Guard row/column tails, use size_t for matrix offsets, and apply alpha/beta once for each valid output.
